All costs are correctly paid (2+2+1 = 5 mana, matching the 5 available lands), all triggers and timing restrictions (equip at sorcery speed, delayed trigger during end step) are properly respected, and the opponent has no way to interact given the unblockable and damage-based effects. This matches the official solution in substance and order.
model_solution:
Main phase 1:
1. Pay {2} (two lands): Equip Stitcher's Graft to The Scorpion God. The Graft becomes unattached from Furyblade Vampire, so the Graft's trigger sacrifices the Vampire. The Scorpion God is now 9/8.
2. Activate Key to the City: tap it and discard Precise Strike, targeting The Scorpion God — it can't be blocked this turn.

Combat:
3. Attack with The Scorpion God only (Skirsdag Supplicant stays home, untapped). It's unblockable and deals 9 damage. Opponent: 11 → 2.

Main phase 2:
4. Pay {2} (two more lands): Equip Stitcher's Graft to Skirsdag Supplicant. The Graft becomes unattached from The Scorpion God, so the Graft's trigger sacrifices The Scorpion God. Its "when this dies" ability triggers: it will return to my hand at the beginning of the next end step.

End step:
5. At the beginning of the end step, The Scorpion God returns to my hand.
6. With my last land (a Swamp or Canyon Slough for {B}), activate Skirsdag Supplicant: {B}, {T}, discard The Scorpion God — each player loses 2 life. Opponent: 2 → 0. Win.

(The opponent has no cards, no mana-relevant actions, and no way to block an unblockable creature, so this works against every possible response.)

comp_rules.txt

Puzzle conventions:
Winning
Unless otherwise stated, you must win the puzzle by inflicting lethal damage to your opponent before the turn ends. This can be as late as during the cleanup step if necessary. Your solution must work for all possible outcomes, such as your opponent’s actions and blocking decisions (see below.)
Phase
Unless otherwise stated, you begin each puzzle at the beginning of your first main phase. You have already drawn a card and gone past upkeep triggers. You have not yet played a land, cast any spells, activated any abilities of permanents on the battlefield, or attacked.
Your Opponent’s Resources / Actions
Unless otherwise stated, your opponent has no cards in hand and no other permanents in play (including no lands – despite the lack of realism there.) This means the only actions you need to consider are activated abilities with no mana cost. Most puzzles with opponent actions will offer more information on this.
Blocking
You cannot assume that your opponent will block a certain way, unless they are somehow forced to. Your solution must satisfy all possible blocking scenarios, even ones that would seem strange in a regular game, and always deal lethal in order to be correct.
Dice
Sometimes you will see six-sided dice placed on cards. These are meant to indicate counters, of whatever type is most reasonable to be there. On most creatures they will be +1/+1 counters, on most artifacts and lands they will be charge counters, and on most Planeswalkers they will be loyalty counters.
If the card specifies a type of counter itself, however (like Icatian Javelineers or Raging Ravine), that will dictate which type it is. 
For -1/-1 counters, we will use a separate graphic to avoid confusion.
Zones
Unless otherwise stated, all zones not displayed are empty. Neither you nor your opponent have cards in graveyards or in exile.
Cards Drawn from Libraries
In any puzzle in which either player might draw cards or otherwise access their library, the puzzle will stipulate some known or assumed information about the library.
Most commonly, this will be a statement that you should assume that the cards remaining in libraries are to be assumed to be irrelevant to the puzzle.
Your Life
Occasionally, your own life total might appear to matter – for cards like Anguished Unmaking, for example. If we require you to consider your own life total in a puzzle, it will be displayed.
If your life total is not shown, you may assume it is irrelevant and effectively infinite.

When you are ready to answer, put your final winning line inside <solution> tags:

<solution>
1. First step...
2. Second step...
</solution>

Your line must be legal under the rules and must win against all possible opponent responses and blocking decisions.

I'm mapping out my resources: Precise Strike in hand, three Canyon Sloughs and two Swamps for five mana with three red sources, Key to the City for unblockable effects, and The Scorpion God's activated ability to shrink creatures and draw cards off -1/-1 counter deaths.

I also note Furyblade Vamp for extra damage via discard, and Skirsdag Supplicant's drain ability.

The opponent sits at 11 life with four blockers: two Grim Flayers, a Hapatra, and a Druid of the Cowl. Killing a 2/2 fully would take two activations, which I can't afford, so I'm weighing whether to counter my own Skirsdag Supplicant or Furyblade Vampire instead to trigger a death draw. I'm mapping out total attacking power — Scorpion God's 6, Furyblade Vampire's 4 or 7 with a discard for trample, and Skirsdag Supplicant's 2 — against the four blockers, and considering using Key to the City (discarding Precise Strike) to make the Scorpion God unblockable for a guaranteed 6, while sending Furyblade Vampire in to trample over whatever combination of blockers gets thrown at it.

Now I'm working out whether Stitcher's Glue equipped onto another creature could sacrifice Furyblade Vampire for a card if it carries a -1/-1 counter, weighing the mana cost against drawing into an unplayed land this turn to fund Skirsdag Supplicant's life-loss ability, which also needs a discard to activate.

Let me instead try attacking first with Key to the City making Scorpion God unblockable for 6 after discarding Precise Strike, then sending in Furyblade Vampire and Supplicant to see how the opponent's four blockers might absorb the rest of the damage.

I'm counting up total possible damage sources, including combat and Supplicant's single activation since it can't untap. Vampire with Key's discard bonus could hit 7/5 unblockable, but that needs two discardable cards while I only have Precise Strike in hand, so I need to find a way to draw an extra card—maybe through Scorpion God's -1/-1 counter trigger.

Sac'ing Vampire to Stitcher's Graft would draw a card but cost me my attacker, so that's a tradeoff. Putting a -1/-1 counter on an opponent's creature during combat draws too late for most discard plays, except Supplicant staying back to activate post-combat for 2 life loss per player using a freshly drawn card. So the plan forming is: use Key to the City, discarding Precise Strike to make Scorpion God unblockable.

Attacking with Scorpion God and Vampire, Scorpion God's 6 damage puts opponent at 5, while I use its ability to shrink a blocker before combat damage so it dies and I draw a card, feeding Supplicant's post-combat discard for another 2 life loss. Running the numbers though, even with trample from Vampire this doesn't quite get opponent low enough, so I'm considering also playing an extra land this turn.

Alternatively, discarding Precise Strike to pump Vampire to 7/5 trample and attacking with everyone leaves the opponent enough blockers to absorb most of the trample damage, so that line falls short too.

I'm also weighing equipping Graft onto Scorpion God, which would sacrifice the Vampire and boost Scorpion God to 9/8, but that costs five mana for one card while giving up a body.

Instead I'm mapping out a sequence using Key to the City on Scorpion God to make it unblockable at 9, combined with Supplicant discarding for 2 more damage, totaling 11 — tracing through the exact mana taps from Canyon Slough and Swamp to see if it lines up.

Then I'm checking the Stitcher's Graft equip step: moving it from Furyblade Vampire to Scorpion God at sorcery speed triggers a sacrifice of the Vampire, which already has a -1/-1 counter, causing it to die and letting me draw a card off Scorpion God's trigger, while Scorpion God grows to 9/8.

But then I run into a mana and card sequencing problem — playing the land drop leaves only Precise Strike in hand, which Key to the City needs to discard for unblockability, but that same card was needed to feed Bloodthirsty Blade's Supplicant discard requirement, and I can't satisfy both with only one card left. I'm now weighing whether to hold the land back instead, though that leaves me short on mana for both the counter activation and the equip cost, so I'm looking for another way to remove the Vampire without relying on the equip trigger.

Reconsidering the total damage math: I need 11 total, and Scorpion God at 9/8 unblockable plus Supplicant's 2-life drain hits exactly that, but the combination costs 3 mana plus two separate cards (one to discard for Key, one to discard for Supplicant), on top of the mana for growing Scorpion God via a -1/-1 counter death trigger. Tallying it all up, I need 6 mana total and I'm one card short of covering both discard costs with just 5 mana and a single spare card in hand.

I'm now testing an alternative line: attacking with Scorpion God (unblockable, 6/5) alongside a 4/5 trample Vampire while leaving Supplicant back, then working through what happens if the Vampire gets through unblocked — that gets the opponent to 1 life, but I still need one more point of damage and no creature has actually died to fuel Scorpion God's growth in that scenario.

Playing that Swamp gives me the black mana to have Supplicant discard it and drain the opponent for 2, using both discard outlets (Precise Strike to Key, Swamp to Supplicant) — bringing total damage to 6 (Scorpion God) + trample damage + 2 (Supplicant), which should be lethal.

I'm now questioning whether the Vampire's death even needs to come from an equip-based combat trick, and considering whether just attacking with the Vampire directly could trigger the draw some other way.

I keep going in circles on how to sequence the Graft equip, the counter, and combat math so that at 11 life the opponent is forced into a specific block that lets a countered blocker die and trigger the draw, since 9 (God) + 2 (Supplicant) exactly equals 11 and forces a block on the Supplicant, leaving me to check if I still have mana left after the equip to counter that blocker post-block.

Every path I trace ends exactly one resource short — either mana, a card, or an untapped creature — so I'm going back to reread Key to the City's full text since I suspect I'm missing an ability or trigger there that unlocks the extra resource I need.

That's the God attacking alone with unblockable analyzed. Trying Graft interactions — equipping Graft to the God during main phase would sacrifice the Vampire, boosting the God's stats before combat.

Then discarding Key to make Precise Strike unblockable and swinging with the God alone, dropping the opponent to 2. After combat there's leftover mana but nothing productive to do with it — putting the counter on Supplicant or the opponent's creature doesn't kill anything useful. Considering instead leaving Vampire back to trade in combat, or using Precise Strike directly on Supplicant to pump it.

Checking Hapatra's trigger again: if I put a -1/-1 counter and give the opponent a snake token, that's actually bad since it hands them another blocker. And with four blockers already up, chumping the God isn't really in question — they'll definitely block if needed. Going back to whether the Vampire trigger plus Key discard can be sequenced pre-combat to draw into something better.

Key doesn't offer any untap-triggered draw, so that's out. Recounting mana sources: Canyon Slough taps for three colors of black or red, plus two Swamps, giving five total. I'm running back through the sequencing for the unblockable line, trying counter placement on Vampire during main phase one and equipping Graft elsewhere.

Equipping Graft to the God costs two mana, and if Vampire dies I draw a Swamp, play it for one black mana, leaving Perilous Skydiver in hand and the God at 9/8. Discarding Skydiver to Key makes the God unblockable, but attacking with both God and Supplicant lets the opponent just block Supplicant, so total damage falls short at only nine unblockable plus a blocked attacker — opponent survives at two life. Trying variations like attacking with only the God, or discarding the Swamp instead to keep Skydiver in hand, all hit the same wall since Supplicant keeps getting blocked and the damage doesn't add up to lethal.

I try flipping which creature gets the counter — putting it on Vampire and equipping Graft to Supplicant instead, making it a 5/6, then discarding Skydiver to Key to make Supplicant unblockable for five damage while the God attacks and gets chumped. That doesn't work either, nor does making the God unblockable at 6 while Supplicant gets chumped. With four blockers on the opponent's side, making just one creature unblockable never seems to add up to the eleven damage needed, so I'm re-checking whether I have the Vampire's combat trigger right — confirming it's discard a card for +3/+0 until end of turn — and looking again for where I might be missing an extra point of damage.

I'm trying to figure out what could die to justify a counter after combat—Druid becomes 1/2, nothing obviously dies unless Supplicant attacks and gets blocked. But that path doesn't seem productive, so I should look for another line entirely.

Rechecking the Scorpion God's activated ability costs three mana, which changes my math. Let me reconsider whether Vampire's trample combined with Precise Strike's first strike and a -1/-1 counter on the blocker could actually make this work.

Trying different attack combinations with God, Vampire, and Supplicant, I'm calculating how much damage gets through depending on how the opponent distributes blockers and whether they use the counter on the Vampire versus leaving something unblocked.

Every configuration I check comes up one point of damage or resource short of lethal, so I'm forced to reconsider whether God truly stays unblockable and whether trample math can somehow double up—maybe through Stitcher's Graft's sacrifice-on-unattach trigger interacting with the creatures in a way that changes the calculus.

The God itself can't be a target for its own counter-move ability, so that's out. Checking the Supplicant math: counter on Vampire drops it to 0/1, still alive after Graft moves off, which then gets sacrificed — that math checks out. Then considering whether Precise Strike could actually be cast rather than discarded: with the counter on Vampire and equip moved to God for the draw, Key discards the Swamp for unblockable, leaving PS in hand with no mana spent yet.

Trying another discard order: play Swamp first, then discard Precise Strike to Key instead — same net result. What if the equip swap happens after combat, leaving God at 6 during combat instead? There's no way to squeeze out a second land drop this turn either.

Reconsidering the combined attack with both God (unblockable via Key, dealing 6) and Vampire with Graft (4/5 trample) — opponent drops to 5 after God's hit, then has to figure out how to survive Vampire's trample given only 5 mana and whatever blockers or tricks they have. Working through the opponent's possible responses: if Vampire goes unblocked, that's 4 more damage putting them at 1.

I need just one more point of damage from somewhere, but I'm stuck: with 5 mana and no cards, using the counter-then-equip trick to try to draw a card from Swamp comes up empty. So I'm now considering also swinging with Supplicant to push total unblocked damage to 12, forcing the opponent into a block. If they block Supplicant with a 2/2, that leaves Vampire's 4 trample getting through, dropping them to 1; if they block Vampire with something like Druid, trample plus Supplicant's 2 still gets them close. With 5 mana available I can counter whatever blocks Supplicant, shrinking it to 1/1 so Supplicant survives and kills it, potentially drawing me a card off Swamp's trigger.

But if the opponent instead dumps all four blockers onto Vampire, leaving Supplicant untapped and unblocked, Vampire dies to the swarm even with a counter buff, and I still only get to 5 damage — one short. I'm second-guessing whether Hapatra could somehow trigger in my favor, but no, that doesn't apply here. I double-check Key to the City's actual wording to make sure I'm not missing an alternate mode. I also consider whether Grim Flayer's delirium interacts with opponent's graveyard fills from their dying creatures, but that only counts creature card types, so it doesn't help. Finally I look at whether a counter spell on a blocker of the God (6/5, not unblockable) could open up lethal that way instead.

I try Precise Strike's first strike bonus against the God (7/5) and it doesn't help either. I keep circling back to the timing puzzle: if I discard cards to both Vampire's trigger and Key pre-combat using a card drawn earlier, the pre-combat draw kills Vampire before combat even starts, ruling that line out — unless some other creature could die pre-combat from a counter instead of Vampire. Testing Supplicant (2/3 → 1/2 with a counter), I can't find a way to actually kill it before combat, and equipping Graft to it just saves Vampire and gets me nowhere.

I keep coming back to Supplicant's activated ability, wondering if it could somehow fire post-combat, but it's tapped from attacking so that's dead unless it had vigilance. I'm also reconsidering whether the God's power, combined with Supplicant connecting unblocked, changes the total damage math, but nothing clicks yet.

Only one Key equip available, so combining God plus Vampire unblockable still doesn't add up to 9 with opponent at 11 life. Let me reconsider whether Scorpion God's card draw trigger fires when a creature with a -1/-1 counter dies, since that could unlock another line.

Playing Swamp instead gives {B} plus Supplicant but no card in hand. What if the counter goes on an opponent's creature instead of the Vampire, so a non-unblockable God trade kills it in combat—but that depends on the opponent's blocking choice, which is unreliable.

Considering whether Supplicant can attack and still drain, but it can't untap that way, so that's a dead end. Rethinking whether Key is even needed if the opponent lacks untapped blockers, but that's not guaranteed either.

I'm reconsidering skipping Key entirely and just attacking with God and Vampire, but the opponent will simply block with a creature that isn't affected by the counter, so only having one counter available limits this line. Rereading the Key and Vampire's actual wording to confirm Key grants unblockable and Vampire has trample, then checking that both Vampire's trigger and Key are free to activate, leaving the mana accounting to the counter placement itself.

Now I'm working through the max-damage combination: getting God to 9 unblockable damage via equip and Key, plus a drain trigger, requires 3 mana and 2 cards, but I only have 5 mana and 1 card, so I need to convert 3 mana into an extra card through a free kill enabled by the counter placed on a blocker — the Graft-equipped Vampire could provide that free death, but the mana still doesn't add up given the equip and drain costs, and the drawn Swamp itself counts as a card rather than a bonus. I'm also considering whether the free kill could instead come from the opponent blocking the Supplicant with the countered creature, but Supplicant would then be tapped and unable to also drain.

I try another angle: attacking with Vampire unsacrificed, letting it get blocked and killed by the counter to draw a card, then equipping Graft to God afterward — but God has already dealt its damage by then, so that doesn't work either. A trampling Vampire plus partial God damage seems too unreliable to count on.

Since standard combos keep falling short, I suspect I'm missing a rules interaction — possibly involving re-equipping Stitcher's Graft between permanents to trigger multiple sacrifices, or overlooked triggers from Scorpion God's draw ability applying to any creature with a -1/-1 counter, not just my own, or something about how Key to the City behaves when it becomes untapped.

I also check first strike combined with trample and a countered blocker, timing the card draw before regular damage, but that doesn't open anything new either. None of the opponent's other permanents like Druid of the Cowl seem relevant since they have no cards in hand. I remind myself the puzzle likely accepts life loss as equivalent to lethal damage, then return to the plan of attacking with an unblockable God and forcing a block on the Supplicant, wondering if there's a way to exploit however that block resolves.

I try putting Key on Supplicant instead, but then God becomes blockable and gets chumped for only 2 damage getting through — that fails. I also consider first strike on God, but that seems irrelevant, and a counter on Vampire making it 3/4 trample doesn't seem to lead anywhere either. Then I think about equipping Graft to God after combat for the sacrifice-draw while Vampire attacks separately, since its damage isn't strictly needed — casting Key first to make God unblockable, then attacking with both God and Vampire.

Working through the damage: after countering Vampire to 3/4 trample and post-combat equipping Graft to sacrifice it and draw a Swamp, I don't end up with a usable card, so that line fails too. I also check whether letting Supplicant through unblocked while Vampire gets blocked changes the math, but the total still isn't enough. I briefly wonder if Key could be discarded at instant speed during declare blockers, but making something unblockable after blocks are already declared is useless.

Reconsidering the God attack line: if God gets chump-blocked it kills the blocker, and if that blocker has a -1/-1 counter, that triggers a draw — but even combining God, Vampire with trample, and Supplicant attacking together, Supplicant ends up tapped and the numbers don't work out. I try approaching this from the puzzle designer's perspective instead, cataloging what each card does: Key turns something unblockable and refills on untap, Scorpion God draws when a countered creature dies and applies -1/-1 counters, and Furyblade has its own ability to factor in.

I list out the remaining pieces — Vampire's discard-for-+3, Stitcher's Graft sacrificing when unattached, Supplicant's discard-drain, Canyon Slough's cycling ability, Precise Strike, and a library of all Swamps — while noting Hapatra and Grim Flayer on the opponent's side seem like red herrings around counters and graveyard synergy that don't actually change my calculations. My best guess at the intended line — countering the Vampire, moving Graft to the God, drawing into a Swamp, then using Key to make the God unblockable for 9 trample damage — comes up exactly one point short, so there must be another piece I'm missing.

I try combining Key on the God with Vampire trample and Supplicant, but that doesn't add up either, and I consider whether Precise Strike granting first strike matters, checking scenarios where the God or Supplicant is blocked by a chump creature. None of these interactions seem to change the outcome, so I lean toward Precise Strike just being discard fodder rather than part of the actual combo.

I also try recounting the land total again, wondering if there's a way to fit in casting Precise Strike alongside the counter and equip sequence, but the mana doesn't work out since PS needs red mana I don't have. I check whether Hapatra could trigger off counters we place ourselves, but under the actual rules that doesn't happen.

I consider whether re-equipping the graft ability to the same creature does anything useful, but that seems like a dead end per the attachment rules. Then I try a different combat sequencing — triggering the vampire's discard of Precise Strike before other steps to see if that opens up a better line.

With the extra Swamp giving 6 total mana, I could double up on counters, but then equipping is out of reach. Any deaths would have to come from combat instead, and two countered creatures dying there would trigger two draws, but the drain effect still needs that extra black mana I don't have — seven total mana required, which doesn't work.

Trying counter plus equip plus drain comes to six mana exactly with five lands and the Swamp, but I'm short a card since the drain needs another piece in hand beyond the Key. Alternatively, counter plus drain alone uses four mana, leaving the Key on the God for six power trampling and one spare mana — but that only lands if the opponent blocks the Vampire with something small enough for trample damage to get through.

I'm also considering casting the discard spell on the Vampire itself to enable Key, but that eats the only spare card. Drawing extra cards during combat isn't feasible without a death trigger already active, so I'm circling back to whether attacking with the God unblockable alongside the Supplicant and using Key differently might open up a cleaner line.

Key to the City doesn't have an untap trigger, so that's a dead end. The Graft creature's attack trigger about not untapping is also irrelevant here. I'm still checking whether there's any way to make the God 9/8 while keeping the Vampire alive, but it doesn't seem possible, so I'm moving on to consider other creatures.

I try Skirsdag Supplicant combined with Graft: Supplicant becomes 5/6 with an unblockable Key equipped, dealing 5, but the God only gets chump blocked, so that fails. Then I consider using the Scorpion God's instant-speed ability during blockers on a creature blocking Supplicant, but Supplicant would already be tapped. Another line: keep Supplicant back, swing with a 9/8 unblockable God to bring the opponent to 2, then post-combat try equipping Graft from the God onto Supplicant, which would cause the God to die from the unattached Graft trigger.

I check whether the God has a -1/-1 counter for its own death trigger, but it doesn't, and I realize sacrificing the God for this line isn't even mana-efficient since it costs more than available. I also consider putting a counter on the dead Vampire, which obviously doesn't work since it's already gone. So I go back to not equipping pre-combat: attack with the unblockable God for 6 and a 4/5 trample Vampire, bringing the opponent to 5, and check whether the Vampire gets blocked or not—if unblocked, that's 4 more damage bringing them to 1, which still isn't lethal, so I look at responding by placing a counter on the Vampire mid-combat to shrink it and see if that changes the damage math enough.

Neither line quite gets there, so I start hunting for a way to pump the Vampire before combat using two available cards while keeping it alive, but the numbers don't work out since I can't find a pre-combat death besides the Vampire itself to generate the needed resources. I consider whether the Supplicant could die instead to free things up, but killing it would take way too much mana. Then I pivot to attacking with all three creatures together, checking if an unblocked scenario across God, Vampire, and Supplicant adds up to lethal damage.

Actually wait, the Graft's mandatory sacrifice trigger requires the Vampire to still be alive to sacrifice — if it's already dead or gone from the board, that clause wouldn't apply the same way.

I try skipping the equip route and check whether the God's unblockable damage plus drain plus other pieces can add up, but that falls short. I also test combining the God's unblockable hit with a trampling pumped Vampire, using counters on blockers to control combat math, and double-check Grim Flayer's delirium bonus — irrelevant since the opponent's graveyard is empty. Druid of the Cowl's stats don't help either, so I keep searching for the right combination.

I wonder if the puzzle's real answer involves reaching 6 mana through the lands in play plus a drawn Swamp, and start questioning whether the Key's discard is even necessary if the God can attack with enough power to overwhelm four blockers. Then I consider whether the Scorpion God's draw trigger fetches the Swamp needed to complete the mana, letting Key discard the Prized Amalgam-like piece while Supplicant still needs a card — but I can't find a second draw source, since neither the Vampire sacrifice trigger nor untapping the Key seem to provide it. I start wondering if placing a counter on the Vampire during combat could be the missing piece.

I keep hitting the same conflict: Key needs a discard, but Precise Strike needs to be cast, and there's only one card to work with — using Key to discard a drawn Swamp only works if Vampire's already dead. So if I want Key active while Vampire lives, Precise Strike has to be the discard, leaving nothing else to cast, and combat just resolves at 6 damage.

Trying the trample math instead: 8 damage plus trample, needing at least 3 trample through to matter, but the opponent can dodge by either not blocking Vampire (pushing 4 trample through for 10 total, no death, no card draw) or double-blocking to prevent damage entirely. I keep looking for a way to force a death in the unblocked line to trigger a draw, but equipping post-combat costs 5 mana and still leaves me short a card after drawing and playing a land — the unblocked scenario just doesn't leave enough resources to close the last point of damage even with the drain.

I'm starting to question my base assumptions: whether Precise Strike could be discarded differently, whether opponent's life total is really 11, whether the God's ability could target something more useful, or whether there's some interaction with Hapatra's trigger I'm missing when she deals combat damage — I need to reread her exact wording about putting -1/-1 counters.

I confirm the -1/-1 counter mechanic and Scorpion God's draw trigger, then reconsider the Vampire's stats with and without Stitcher's Graft equipped, wondering if there's another way to force its death by manipulating the counter and moving the Graft off it.

Actually, I realize the key insight: if the God dies while its owner controls fewer than devotion 5, it returns to its owner's hand at the beginning of the next end step. That means it becomes a card in hand exactly during the end step, letting the Supplicant discard it then to trigger a life drain — explaining how the puzzle's win condition can trigger as late as cleanup.

Working through the sequence: equipping Graft to the God first sacrifices the Vampire, then attacking with the unblockable God for 9 brings the opponent to 2. Then moving Graft onto Supplicant sacrifices the God itself, which returns to hand at the next end step — at which point I can discard it to the Supplicant using my last mana to drain the final 2 life.

The end step timing works fine, even allowing cleanup step if needed. Supplicant stays untapped since it didn't attack, and Key is necessary to make God unblockable for the full 9 damage while discarding it. Opponent has no way to interfere since they have no available actions.

Moving to the equip sequence: attaching Graft to God unattaches it from Vampire, sacrificing Vampire, then re-equipping Graft to Supplicant in main phase 2 unattaches it from God, sacrificing God — which triggers its delayed return at the next end step. Mana totals easily cover the costs (8 available versus 5 needed), so no additional counter placement on Vampire is required.

input.pattern: beginning of the next end step

713:Example: Mimic Vat has a triggered ability whose effect gives you the option to exile a card and an activated ability that says “Create a token that’s a copy of a card exiled with this artifact. It gains haste. Exile it at the beginning of the next end step.” If no card has been exiled with Mimic Vat’s triggered ability, no token is created.
2428:513.1a Previously, abilities that triggered at the beginning of the end step were printed with the trigger condition “at end of turn.” Cards that were printed with that text have received errata in the Oracle card reference to say “at the beginning of the end step” or “at the beginning of the next end step.”
2430:513.2. If a permanent with an ability that triggers “at the beginning of the end step” enters the battlefield during this step, that ability won’t trigger until the next turn’s end step. Likewise, if a delayed triggered ability that triggers “at the beginning of the next end step” is created during this step, that ability won’t trigger until the next turn’s end step. In other words, the step doesn’t “back up” so those abilities can go on the stack. This rule applies only to triggered abilities; it doesn’t apply to continuous effects whose durations say “until end of turn” or “this turn.” (See rule 514, “Cleanup Step.”)
2615:Example: An ability that reads “Exile this creature at the beginning of the next end step” will exile the permanent even if it’s no longer a creature during the next end step. However, it won’t do anything if the permanent left the battlefield before then.
3240:Example: An ability reads “Target creature gets +2/+2 until end of turn. Destroy that creature at the beginning of the next end step.” The ability will destroy the object it gave +2/+2 to even if that object isn’t a creature at the beginning of the next end step.
4602:702.84a Unearth is an activated ability that functions while the card with unearth is in a graveyard. “Unearth [cost]” means “[Cost]: Return this card from your graveyard to the battlefield. It gains haste. Exile it at the beginning of the next end step. If it would leave the battlefield, exile it instead of putting it anywhere else. Activate only as a sorcery.”
4792:702.109a Dash represents three abilities: two static abilities that function while the card with dash is on the stack, one of which may create a delayed triggered ability, and a static ability that functions while the object with dash is on the battlefield. “Dash [cost]” means “You may cast this card by paying [cost] rather than its mana cost,” “If this spell’s dash cost was paid, return the permanent this spell becomes to its owner’s hand at the beginning of the next end step,” and “As long as this permanent’s dash cost was paid, it has haste.” Casting a spell for its dash cost follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.
5026:702.141a Encore is an activated ability that functions while the card with encore is in a graveyard. “Encore [cost]” means “[Cost], Exile this card from your graveyard: For each opponent, create a token that’s a copy of this card that attacks that opponent this turn if able. The tokens gain haste. Sacrifice them at the beginning of the next end step. Activate only as a sorcery.”
5104:702.152a Blitz represents three abilities: two static abilities that function while the card with blitz is on the stack, one of which may create a delayed triggered ability, and a static ability that functions while the object with blitz is on the battlefield. “Blitz [cost]” means “You may cast this card by paying [cost] rather than its mana cost,” “If this spell’s blitz cost was paid, sacrifice the permanent this spell becomes at the beginning of the next end step,” and “As long as this permanent’s blitz cost was paid, it has haste and ‘When this permanent is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, draw a card.’” Casting a spell for its blitz cost follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.
5340:702.181a Mobilize is a triggered ability. “Mobilize N” means “Whenever this creature attacks, create N 1/1 red Warrior creature tokens. Those tokens enter tapped and attacking. Sacrifice them at the beginning of the next end step.”
5361:702.185a Warp represents two static abilities that function while the card with warp is on the stack, one of which may create a delayed triggered ability. “Warp [cost]” means “You may cast this card from your hand by paying [cost] rather than its mana cost” and “If this spell’s warp cost was paid, exile the permanent this spell becomes at the beginning of the next end step. Its owner may cast this card after the current turn has ended for as long as it remains exiled.” Casting a spell for its warp cost follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.
5903:Example: Otherworldly Journey is an instant that reads “Exile target creature. At the beginning of the next end step, return that card to the battlefield under its owner’s control with a +1/+1 counter on it.” A player casts Otherworldly Journey targeting Chittering Host, a melded permanent. Chittering Host is exiled. At the beginning of the next end step, Midnight Scavengers and Graf Rats are both returned to the battlefield, each with a +1/+1 counter on it.
6389:Example: Astral Slide is an enchantment that reads, “Whenever a player cycles a card, you may exile target creature. If you do, return that creature to the battlefield under its owner’s control at the beginning of the next end step.” During Alex’s turn, Bianca uses Astral Slide’s ability to exile Alex’s Hypnotic Specter. Before the end of that turn, Bianca leaves the game. At the beginning of the end step, the delayed triggered ability generated by Astral Slide that would return Hypnotic Specter to the battlefield triggers, but it isn’t put on the stack. Hypnotic Specter never returns to the battlefield.
7179:A trigger condition printed on abilities that triggered at the beginning of the end step (which is not the last thing to happen in the turn). Cards that were printed with that text have received errata in the Oracle card reference to say “at the beginning of the end step” or “at the beginning of the next end step.” See rule 513, “End Step.”
8315:A keyword ability that creates a number of tapped and attacking red Warrior creature tokens that are sacrificed at the beginning of the next end step. See rule 702.181, “Mobilize.”

3279:701.3a To attach an Aura, Equipment, or Fortification to an object or player means to take it from where it currently is and put it onto that object or player. If something is attached to a permanent on the battlefield, it’s customary to place it so that it’s physically touching the permanent. An Aura, Equipment, or Fortification can’t be attached to an object or player it couldn’t enchant, equip, or fortify, respectively.
3281:701.3b If an effect tries to attach an Aura, Equipment, or Fortification to an object or player it can’t be attached to, the Aura, Equipment, or Fortification doesn’t move. If an effect tries to attach an Aura, Equipment, or Fortification to the object or player it’s already attached to, the effect does nothing. If an effect tries to attach an object that isn’t an Aura, Equipment, or Fortification to another object or player, the effect does nothing and the first object doesn’t move.
3283:701.3c Attaching an Aura, Equipment, or Fortification on the battlefield to a different object or player causes the Aura, Equipment, or Fortification to receive a new timestamp.
3285:701.3d To “unattach” an Equipment from a creature means to move it away from that creature so the Equipment is on the battlefield but is not equipping anything. It should no longer be physically touching any creature. If an Aura, Equipment, or Fortification that was attached to an object or player ceases to be attached to it, that counts as “becoming unattached [from that object or player]”; this includes if that Aura, Equipment, or Fortification leaves the battlefield, the object leaves the zone it was in, or that player leaves the game.

The key insight is that The Scorpion God's death trigger ("return it to its owner's hand at the beginning of the next end step") gives me an extra card in hand at the end step — exactly the second discard I need for Skirsdag Supplicant. Stitcher's Graft both pumps the God to a 9/8 and later kills it on demand when I move the equipment again (rule 701.3d: moving it counts as "becoming unattached").

Mana check: 5 lands = Equip {2} + Equip {2} + Supplicant {B}. Cards: Precise Strike → Key to the City; The Scorpion God (returned) → Supplicant.

<solution>
Main phase 1:
1. Pay {2} (two lands): Equip Stitcher's Graft to The Scorpion God. The Graft becomes unattached from Furyblade Vampire, so the Graft's trigger sacrifices the Vampire. The Scorpion God is now 9/8.
2. Activate Key to the City: tap it and discard Precise Strike, targeting The Scorpion God — it can't be blocked this turn.

Combat:
3. Attack with The Scorpion God only (Skirsdag Supplicant stays home, untapped). It's unblockable and deals 9 damage. Opponent: 11 → 2.

Main phase 2:
4. Pay {2} (two more lands): Equip Stitcher's Graft to Skirsdag Supplicant. The Graft becomes unattached from The Scorpion God, so the Graft's trigger sacrifices The Scorpion God. Its "when this dies" ability triggers: it will return to my hand at the beginning of the next end step.

End step:
5. At the beginning of the end step, The Scorpion God returns to my hand.
6. With my last land (a Swamp or Canyon Slough for {B}), activate Skirsdag Supplicant: {B}, {T}, discard The Scorpion God — each player loses 2 life. Opponent: 2 → 0. Win.

(The opponent has no cards, no mana-relevant actions, and no way to block an unblockable creature, so this works against every possible response.)
</solution>
